title.en: Investment; ex ante and ex post

body.en: Investment is the addition to the stock of physical capital (machines, buildings, roads) and to inventories in a year. In this short-run model, planned investment is taken as autonomous: $I = \bar{I}$, not depending on income. Ex ante values are planned values; ex post values are actual, realised values. Planned and actual values can differ; the difference shows up as unplanned changes in inventories.

points.en: Investment: addition to capital stock and inventories
Planned investment is autonomous: I = Ī
Ex ante = planned; ex post = actual
Gap appears as unplanned inventory change

narration.kn: ಹೂಡಿಕೆ ಎಂದರೆ ಒಂದು ವರ್ಷದಲ್ಲಿ ಭೌತಿಕ ಬಂಡವಾಳ ಮತ್ತು ದಾಸ್ತಾನಿಗೆ ಆಗುವ ಸೇರ್ಪಡೆ. ಈ ಮಾದರಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಯೋಜಿತ ಹೂಡಿಕೆ ಸ್ವಾಯತ್ತ: I = Ī. ಪೂರ್ವನಿಯೋಜಿತ (ex ante) ಎಂದರೆ ಯೋಜಿತ ಮೌಲ್ಯ; ಉತ್ತರಕಾಲೀನ (ex post) ಎಂದರೆ ನಿಜವಾದ ಮೌಲ್ಯ. ಎರಡರ ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸ ಯೋಜಿತವಲ್ಲದ ದಾಸ್ತಾನು ಬದಲಾವಣೆಯಾಗಿ ಕಾಣುತ್ತದೆ.

title.en: On the board: Equilibrium on the Keynesian cross

narration.en: Equilibrium income is where aggregate demand equals output, shown on the Keynesian cross.

say.en: Aggregate demand is autonomous spending plus induced consumption. Take C̄ + Ī = 100 and MPC = 0.8.
Output is in equilibrium where the AD line cuts the 45 degree line, at 500.
To the left of E, demand is more than output: stocks fall, so firms produce more.
To the right of E, demand is less than output: unsold stocks pile up, so firms cut output.
Now the algebra. Set output equal to aggregate demand and solve for Y.
At equilibrium, planned saving also equals planned investment.

title.en: Equilibrium income: AD = output and S = I

body.en: Firms produce what they expect to sell. Output is in equilibrium when planned aggregate demand equals planned output (aggregate supply): $Y = \bar{C} + \bar{I} + cY$, giving $Y^* = (\bar{C} + \bar{I})/(1 - c)$. Equivalently, planned saving equals planned investment. If AD > output, inventories fall below plan and output rises; if AD < output, unplanned inventories pile up and output falls. Ex post saving and investment are always equal.

points.en: Same as planned S = planned I
AD > Y: stocks fall, output rises
AD < Y: stocks pile up, output falls

narration.kn: ಯೋಜಿತ ಸಮಗ್ರ ಬೇಡಿಕೆ ಯೋಜಿತ ಉತ್ಪಾದನೆಗೆ ಸಮವಾದಾಗ ಸಮತೋಲನ: Y* = (C̄ + Ī)/(1 − c). ಅಂದರೆ ಯೋಜಿತ ಉಳಿತಾಯ = ಯೋಜಿತ ಹೂಡಿಕೆ. AD ಹೆಚ್ಚಿದ್ದರೆ ದಾಸ್ತಾನು ಕಡಿಮೆಯಾಗಿ ಉತ್ಪಾದನೆ ಏರುತ್ತದೆ; AD ಕಡಿಮೆ ಇದ್ದರೆ ದಾಸ್ತಾನು ಹೆಚ್ಚಿ ಉತ್ಪಾದನೆ ಇಳಿಯುತ್ತದೆ.

caption.en: The circular flow: saving leaks out of the flow and investment is injected back into it.

narration.en: Watch the circular flow. Saving by households is a leakage; investment by firms is an injection. Income is steady only when the two are equal.

tryThis.en: Find the leakage and the injection in the flow.
What happens to the flow if planned investment is more than planned saving?

caption.en: AD = C̄ + Ī + cY (yellow) against the 45° line (white). Equilibrium is where they cross.

narration.en: Move autonomous consumption, investment and the MPC. Read off the equilibrium income and check that saving equals investment there.

tryThis.en: Change Ī and check that saving at Y* always equals Ī.
Raise the MPC to 0.9. Why does Y* rise so much?

body.en: Unplanned inventories are the signal. Stocks falling means demand is ahead of output, so output rises. Stocks piling up means demand is behind, so output falls. Output stops changing only when AD = Y.

mnemonic.en: Stocks fall, output climbs; stocks pile, output declines.

narration.en: A quick way to remember the adjustment: let the godown speak. Stocks fall, output climbs; stocks pile, output declines.

problem.en: In an economy C = 50 + 0.75Y and planned investment I = ₹100 crore. Find the equilibrium income, consumption and saving at equilibrium.

steps.en: Check: S = 100 = I, so planned saving equals planned investment.

answer.en: Y* = ₹600 crore, C = ₹500 crore, S = ₹100 crore (= I).
